paper_metadata.title: Quantum-enhanced analysis of discrete stochastic processes

summary: The paper presents two IBM Q proof-of-principle experiments on the ibmqx2 superconducting device: one for European call option Delta estimation and one for a correlated random walk characteristic function. The reported settings include 8129 shots per characteristic-function evaluation for the option example and 32786 shots for the correlated random walk, with Fourier truncation L=100 and period P=100 in both cases; the claimed quantum benefit is theoretical quadratic speedup via amplitude estimation, not demonstrated practical advantage.

experiments.description: Proof-of-principle IBM quantum cloud experiment for estimating the Delta of a European call option via characteristic-function evaluation and Fourier approximation.

algorithm.variant: Characteristic-function estimation with Pauli X/Y measurement; Fourier-series approximation of option Delta; includes a direct-measurement scheme and an AE-enhanced scheme

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary random-walk increments are encoded on index qubits; data qubit undergoes controlled Rz rotations to accumulate the characteristic function phase. Fourier coefficients are used to reconstruct the Delta from characteristic-function samples.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[f(S_t)] for the European call option Delta function f(St)=Phi((ln(St/K)+(r+sigma^2/2)(T-t))/(sigma*sqrt(T-t))) using Fourier approximation of f and characteristic-function evaluations of the underlying stochastic process.

problem_instance.description: European call option Delta under a geometric Brownian motion model approximated by a discrete random walk.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic stochastic process with parameters mu=0, sigma=0.02, r=0.02, S0=100, t=1, T=10; strike prices swept over a range for evaluation.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Geometric Brownian motion approximated by a random walk via Donsker’s invariance principle; Fourier approximation of the Delta function with period P=100 and truncation L=100.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical curve compared against IBM Q experiment and qiskit noise-model simulation; experiments run for selected strike prices with error mitigation.

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: standard error mitigation protocol available in qiskit

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM superconducting device connectivity (ibmqx2 / ibmq_ourense layout considerations)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical Fourier-series reconstruction from characteristic-function samples; noise-model simulation for comparison.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Assemble Delta from sampled characteristic-function values; compare to theoretical values and noise-model simulation.

results.value: high accuracy in the most important region (strike prices 100 to 150)

speedup_claims.conditions: when using quantum amplitude estimation for characteristic-function estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the AE-enhanced scheme can reduce the approximation error to O(1/2^m) with m ancillas, but the reported IBM experiment uses the direct Pauli-measurement scheme and does not demonstrate AE experimentally.

speedup_claims.conditions: for Fourier approximation of the Delta using L characteristic-function points and N shots per experiment
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a resource-scaling statement, not a measured wall-clock speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(LN) experiments for Fourier approximation; direct Pauli-measurement scheme converges as O(1/sqrt(N_S)) per characteristic-function point; AE can improve to O(1/2^m) amplitude error with m ancillas
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: For each characteristic-function point: n Hadamard gates, n bit-flips, 2n controlled-Rz gates; AE variant adds m ancillas, O(poly(m)) Grover-like iterators, and O(m^2) QFT gates

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: IBM ibmqx2 superconducting QPU; 8129 shots per characteristic-function evaluation; L=100, P=100; direct scheme uses n Hadamards, n bit-flips, and 2n controlled-Rz gates, while AE adds m ancillas and O(poly(m)) Grover-like iterators
limiting_factors: No classical runtime benchmark showing end-to-end superiority
Quadratic speedup is only claimed for the AE variant
Hardware noise and error mitigation dominate the small-device experiment
Characteristic-function sampling still requires many circuit evaluations across v values

notes: Hardware type reported as IBM ibmqx2 superconducting device.

Number of qubits is not given as a single total for the experiment; inferred from the text that the implementation uses n index qubits plus 1 data qubit, but the exact n used in the experiment is not specified, so num_qubits remains null in the resource block and the inference is only qualitative.
Circuit depth is not explicitly quantified; only gate counts and asymptotic scaling are reported.
Speedup order is taken from the paper's claim that AE provides quadratic speed-up over classical Monte Carlo.
The paper reports proof-of-principle IBM Q experiments and theoretical quadratic speedup claims via amplitude estimation, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical methods.

experiments.description: Proof-of-principle IBM quantum cloud experiment for estimating the characteristic function of a correlated random walk with path-dependent increments.

algorithm.variant: Characteristic-function estimation for a first-order correlated random walk; direct Pauli-measurement scheme with optional AE framework

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Index qubits encode the path probabilities of the correlated random walk; controlled Ry rotations implement path dependence between successive steps; a data qubit is used to extract the characteristic function.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the characteristic function of the correlated random walk, i.e., E[e^{ivS_n}], by measuring Pauli observables on the data qubit after path-dependent state preparation.

problem_instance.description: Correlated random walk with two possible increments and step-dependent persistence parameters.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic CRW with increments +1 and -1, initial value x0=0, persistence parameters p_l=(1/2,2/3,5/6,1) and q_l=(1/2,1/3,1/6,0).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Path-dependent index-state preparation using controlled Ry gates conditioned on previous-step index qubits.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Characteristic function evaluated at v_l=2πl/P for l=-L,...,L; theoretical values compared with IBM Q experiment and qiskit noise-model simulation.

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: standard error mitigation protocol available in qiskit

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical simulation of the quantum algorithm with qiskit noise model; manual aggregation of multiple identical experiments due to shot limits.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Assemble characteristic-function plots from measured values and compare to theory/noise-model simulation.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the CRW experiment with direct measurement and error mitigation; AE is discussed as a possible enhancement but not experimentally shown.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(kD_q) circuit depth for qth-order Markov dependence; for the reported first-order CRW, controlled rotations scale linearly with the number of steps
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: For the reported CRW example, path-dependent controlled rotations are applied between successive index qubits; exact gate counts not reported

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: IBM ibmqx2 superconducting QPU; 32786 shots per characteristic-function evaluation; first-order path-dependent controlled-Ry preparation; asymptotic O(kD_q) circuit depth
limiting_factors: No classical end-to-end baseline demonstrating quantum superiority
Only a small correlated random walk instance is experimentally shown
Noise and shot overhead are substantial
AE is optional and not shown as an experimentally realized advantage

notes: Hardware type reported as IBM ibmqx2 superconducting device.
The paper does not state the total qubit count used in the CRW experiment; only the structure of index qubits plus a data qubit is described, so the exact total is not reported.
Circuit depth is not numerically specified; only asymptotic scaling and gate structure are described.
Speedup order is based on the paper's general claim that AE yields quadratic improvement over classical Monte Carlo.
The paper presents a proof-of-principle correlated random walk experiment on IBM Q and discusses theoretical quadratic improvement, but does not establish practical advantage.
